overview:
The Process Check lets you:
- Collect resource usage metrics for specific running processes on any host. For example, CPU, memory, I/O, and number of threads.
- Use [Process Monitors][1] to configure thresholds for how many instances of a specific process should be running and get alerts when the thresholds aren't met (see **Service Checks** below).

**Minimum Agent version:** 6.0.0

[1]: https://docs.datadoghq.com/monitors/create/types/process_check/?tab=checkalert
setup:
### Installation

The Process check is included in the [Datadog Agent][2] package, so you don't need to install anything else on your server.

### Configuration

Unlike many checks, the Process check doesn't monitor anything useful by default. You must configure which processes you want to monitor.

While there's no standard default check configuration, here's an example `process.d/conf.yaml` that monitors SSH/SSHD processes. See the [sample process.d/conf.yaml][3] for all available configuration options. For regex-based process matching, see [Process matching](#process-matching).

```yaml
init_config:
instances:
  - name: ssh
    search_string:
      - ssh
      - sshd
```

**Note**: After you make configuration changes, make sure you [restart the Agent][4].

Retrieving some process metrics requires the Datadog collector to either run as the monitored process user or with privileged access. For the `open_file_descriptors` metric on Unix platforms, there is an additional configuration option. Setting `try_sudo` to `true` in your `conf.yaml` file allows the Process check to try using `sudo` to collect the `open_file_descriptors` metric. Using this configuration option requires setting the appropriate sudoers rules in `/etc/sudoers`:

```shell
dd-agent ALL=NOPASSWD: /bin/ls /proc/*/fd/
```

#### Process matching

By default, the Process check matches processes by exact name. Set `exact_match` to `false` to match using substrings instead.

When `exact_match` is `false`, values in `search_string` are interpreted as Python regular expressions using `re.search()`. Regex metacharacters (`. + * ? ( ) [ ] { } ^ $ | \`) must be escaped with a backslash for literal matching.

For example, to match the literal path `/usr/lib/jdk-11.0.10+9/bin/java`, escape the `.` and `+` characters:

Unescaped (does not match literally):

```yaml
instances:
  - exact_match: false
    name: java_jdk11
    search_string:
      - /usr/lib/jdk-11.0.10+9/bin/java
```

Escaped (matches literally):

```yaml
instances:
  - exact_match: false
    name: java_jdk11
    search_string:
      - /usr/lib/jdk-11\.0\.10\+9/bin/java
```

### Validation

Run the [Agent's status subcommand][5] and look for `process` under the Checks section.

### Metrics notes

The following metrics are not available on Linux or macOS:
- Process I/O metrics are **not** available on Linux or macOS since the files that the Agent reads (`/proc/<PID>/io`) are only readable by the process's owner. For more information, [read the Agent FAQ][6].

The following metrics are not available on Windows:
- `system.cpu.iowait`
- `system.processes.mem.page_faults.minor_faults`
- `system.processes.mem.page_faults.children_minor_faults`
- `system.processes.mem.page_faults.major_faults`
- `system.processes.mem.page_faults.children_major_faults`
- `system.processes.mem.real`

**Note**: Use a [WMI check][11] to gather page fault metrics on Windows.

**Note**: In v6.11+ on Windows, the Agent runs as `ddagentuser` instead of `Local System`. Because of [this][12], it does not have access to the full command line of processes running under other users and to the user of other users' processes. This causes the following options of the check to not work:
- `exact_match` when set to `false`
- `user`, which allows selecting processes that belong to a specific user

All metrics are per `instance` configured in process.yaml, and are tagged `process_name:<instance_name>`.

The `system.processes.cpu.pct` metric sent by this check is only accurate for processes that live for more 
than 30 seconds. Do not expect its value to be accurate for shorter-lived processes.

For the full list of metrics, see the [Metrics section](#metrics).

metrics.name: system.processes.cpu.pct
metrics.description: The CPU utilization of a process.

metrics.name: system.processes.cpu.normalized_pct
metrics.description: The normalized CPU utilization of a process.

metrics.name: system.processes.involuntary_ctx_switches
metrics.description: The number of involuntary context switches performed by this process.

metrics.name: system.processes.ioread_bytes
metrics.description: The number of bytes read from disk by this process. In Windows: the number of bytes read.

metrics.name: system.processes.ioread_bytes_count
metrics.description: The number of bytes read from disk by this process. In Windows: the number of bytes read.

metrics.name: system.processes.ioread_count
metrics.description: The number of disk reads by this process. In Windows: the number of reads by this process.

metrics.name: system.processes.iowrite_bytes
metrics.description: The number of bytes written to disk by this process. In Windows: the number of bytes written by this process.

metrics.name: system.processes.iowrite_bytes_count
metrics.description: The number of bytes written to disk by this process. In Windows: the number of bytes written by this process.

metrics.name: system.processes.iowrite_count
metrics.description: The number of disk writes by this process. In Windows: the number of writes by this process.

metrics.name: system.processes.mem.page_faults.minor_faults
metrics.description: In Unix/Linux and macOS: The number of minor page faults per second for this process.

metrics.name: system.processes.mem.page_faults.children_minor_faults
metrics.description: In Unix/Linux and macOS: The number of minor page faults per second for children of this process.

metrics.name: system.processes.mem.page_faults.major_faults
metrics.description: In Unix/Linux and macOS: The number of major page faults per second for this process.

metrics.name: system.processes.mem.page_faults.children_major_faults
metrics.description: In Unix/Linux and macOS: The number of major page faults per second for children of this process.

metrics.name: system.processes.mem.pct
metrics.description: The process memory consumption.

metrics.name: system.processes.mem.real
metrics.description: The non-swapped physical memory a process has used and cannot be shared with another process (Linux only).

metrics.name: system.processes.mem.rss
metrics.description: The non-swapped physical memory a process has used. aka "Resident Set Size".

metrics.name: system.processes.mem.vms
metrics.description: The total amount of virtual memory used by the process. aka "Virtual Memory Size".

metrics.name: system.processes.number
metrics.description: The number of processes.

metrics.name: system.processes.open_file_descriptors
metrics.description: The number of file descriptors used by this process (only available for processes run as the dd-agent user)

metrics.name: system.processes.open_handles
metrics.description: The number of handles used by this process.

metrics.name: system.processes.threads
metrics.description: The number of threads used by this process.

metrics.name: system.processes.voluntary_ctx_switches
metrics.description: The number of voluntary context switches performed by this process.

metrics.name: system.processes.run_time.avg
metrics.description: The average running time of all instances of this process

metrics.name: system.processes.run_time.max
metrics.description: The longest running time of all instances of this process

metrics.name: system.processes.run_time.min
metrics.description: The shortest running time of all instances of this process

serviceChecks.name: Process Up
serviceChecks.description: Returns OK if the check is within the warning thresholds, CRITICAL if it's outside of the critical thresholds, and WARNING if it's outside of the warning thresholds.

releaseNotes.notes:
***Changed***:

* Reject `thresholds` values at configuration load that the check misread, crashed on, ignored, or would breach for every process count (numeric strings such as `'5'` or `'inf'`, booleans, NaN, a positive infinite lower bound, a negative infinite upper bound, a lower bound above the upper bound, or an infinite value past the two bounds), so an instance with such a value now fails to load and sends no metrics instead of running. ([#25422](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/25422))

***Fixed***:

* Accept the `.inf` string for an unbounded `thresholds` upper bound so it survives JSON transport from Remote Config, and treat an explicit `null` threshold range as the default instead of crashing the check run. ([#25422](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/25422))

***Fixed***:

* Explicitly declare `warning`/`critical` as named properties of the `thresholds` option so it can be validated when configured remotely via Fleet Automation. ([#25140](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/25140))
* Fix `collect_children` failing to collect any child processes when a single pid on the system is inaccessible (eg. `AccessDenied`). ([#25367](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/25367))

***Fixed***:

* Clarify ``exact_match`` behavior for ``search_string``, including the required file extension on Windows. ([#24560](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/24560))

***Added***:

* Add support for security validation in models ([#23109](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/23109))

***Added***:

* Add `enable_legacy_tags_normalization` option to preserve hyphens in tag values when set to false. ([#22303](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/22303))

***Added***:

* Bump minimum version of datadog-checks-base to 37.24.0 ([#21945](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/21945))

***Added***:

* Bump Python to 3.13 ([#21161](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/21161))
* Bump datadog-checks-base to 37.21.0 ([#21477](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/21477))

***Added***:

* Add `reset_cache_on_process_changes` configuration option to control when the shared process list cache is reset ([#20570](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/20570))

***Removed***:

* Remove support for Python 2. ([#18580](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/18580))

***Fixed***:

* Bump the version of datadog-checks-base to 37.0.0 ([#18617](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/18617))

***Changed***:

* Bump minimum version of base check ([#18733](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/18733))

***Added***:

* Bump the python version from 3.11 to 3.12 ([#18212](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/18212))
* Upgrade psutil to 6.0.0 to fix performance issues addressed ([#18688](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/18688))

***Added***:

* Add `use_oneshot` parameter to speed up check runs with `psutil.Process().oneshot()` ([#17817](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/17817))
